Everyday English Vocabulary & Speaking 
 10 Chapters for Building Stronger English 
 About This Course: 
 This course will help you  understand more English and speak more 
 naturally and confidently  . 
 You already know many common English words, such as  happy, busy, 
 interesting, important,  and  difficult  . Now it is time to learn vocabulary that 
 will help you  express your ideas more clearly and exactly  . 
 For example, instead of always saying: 
 “My job is difficult.” 
 you can say: 
 “My job is demanding.” 
 “My job is challenging.” 
 Instead of: 
 “My neighborhood is nice.” 
 you can say: 
 “My neighborhood is peaceful.” 
 “My neighborhood is lively.” 
 “My neighborhood has a friendly atmosphere.” 
 Learning words like these will make your English more natural and give you 
 more choices when you speak.

Why Are We Learning This Vocabulary? 
 The vocabulary in this course was chosen for three important reasons. 
 1. These words are useful in real life. 
 You can use these words when talking about your home, work, friends, 
 hobbies, food, shopping, travel and other everyday subjects. 
 These are words that English speakers regularly use in conversations. 
 2. The words are challenging, but not too difficult. 
 You do not need to learn very advanced or academic vocabulary yet. 
 It is more useful to learn words that you can  understand, remember and 
 actually use when you speak  . 
 For example: 
 good → suitable 
 very tired → exhausted 
 not too expensive → affordable 
 easy to use or reach → convenient 
 someone you can depend on → reliable 
 The goal is not to use the most difficult English word. The goal is to  choose 
 the right word and use it correctly  . 
 3. This vocabulary will help you prepare for IELTS in the future. 
 You may take the IELTS exam later, so we will begin practicing with 
 common  IELTS Speaking Part 1 topics  . 
 IELTS Speaking Part 1 includes questions about familiar subjects such as 
 your home, job, hobbies, friends, food, weekends, shopping, weather, 
 travel and music.

You do  not  need to prepare for the IELTS exam seriously yet. 
 For now, these topics give you an excellent way to practice everyday 
 conversation while slowly building the vocabulary and speaking skills that 
 you will need for IELTS later. 
 The 10 Chapters 
 Chapter 1 — Home & Neighborhood 
 Learn to describe where you live and the area around your home. 
 Vocabulary includes:  spacious, convenient, peaceful, lively, 
 surroundings, suitable, atmosphere 
 Chapter 2 — Work 
 Learn to describe your job, responsibilities, schedule and feelings about 
 work. 
 Vocabulary includes:  demanding, flexible, efficient, responsibility, 
 motivated, routine, challenging 
 Chapter 3 — Hobbies & Free Time 
 Learn to talk about how you spend your free time and the activities you 
 enjoy. 
 Vocabulary includes:  creative, active, passionate, entertaining, 
 productive, recharge, take up 
 Chapter 4 — Friends 
 Learn to describe people's personalities, friendships and relationships. 
 Vocabulary includes:  sincere, reliable, supportive, considerate, 
 outgoing, reserved, have in common

Chapter 5 — Food & Cooking 
 Learn to describe food, eating habits and your food preferences. 
 Vocabulary includes:  appetite, filling, flavor, fresh, balanced, traditional, 
 tempting 
 Chapter 6 — Weekends & Daily Life 
 Learn to talk about your normal routine and how you spend your weekends. 
 Vocabulary includes:  productive, exhausted, energetic, spontaneous, 
 typical, occasionally, make the most of 
 Chapter 7 — Shopping 
 Learn to talk about prices, products and the things you choose to buy. 
 Vocabulary includes:  affordable, reasonable, quality, practical, 
 essential, brand, worth it 
 Chapter 8 — Weather & Seasons 
 Learn to describe different kinds of weather and how weather affects your 
 life. 
 Vocabulary includes:  humid, mild, freezing, pleasant, unpredictable, 
 forecast, affect 
 Chapter 9 — Travel & Holidays 
 Learn to describe trips, destinations and travel experiences. 
 Vocabulary includes:  destination, memorable, adventurous, crowded, 
 scenery, explore, get away 
 Chapter 10 — Music 
 Learn to talk about the music you enjoy and explain your musical 
 preferences.

Vocabulary includes:  taste, lyrics, catchy, relaxing, live, talented, 
 remind 
 How Each Chapter Works 
 Each chapter begins with  seven useful vocabulary words  . 
 For every word, you will see: 
 WORD → SIMPLE DEFINITION → EXAMPLE SENTENCE 
 Do not only memorize the definition. 
 You should practice using the word in a sentence about  your own life  . 
 For example: 
 reliable 
 Meaning: someone you can depend on 
 Example: My best friend is very reliable. 
 Now make it personal: 
 Who is a reliable person in your life? Why are they reliable? 
 At the end of each chapter, you will complete vocabulary exercises and 
 answer speaking questions. 
 Some of the speaking questions are similar to questions you may hear in 
 IELTS Speaking Part 1  in the future. 
 Your Speaking Goal 
 When you answer a question, don't try to give a long or complicated 
 answer.

Start with  2–3 good sentences  . 
 Question: 
 Do you like your neighborhood? 
 Basic answer: 
 Yes. I like my neighborhood. It is nice. 
 Stronger answer: 
 Yes, I do. It's a peaceful neighborhood, but there are plenty of shops 
 nearby, so it's also very convenient. 
 The second answer is not much longer. 
 The difference is that it uses  more specific vocabulary  . 
 That is one of our main goals in this course: 
 Don't try to speak with the most difficult English. 
 Try to speak with more specific, natural and useful English. 
 As you complete the ten chapters, you will build a vocabulary that you can 
 use in  real conversations now  and in  IELTS Speaking later  .
